name: Le Carmin
tier: THE BERTHS · THE SERIOUS DINNERS — TWO STARS INSIDE THE WALLS AND A CHARCOAL COUNTER
recognition: One MICHELIN star, still shown on its MICHELIN page after the France 2026 selection (16 March 2026); Gault&Millau 2026: 13/20
what_to_order: Lunch menu, 3 or 4 courses|Foie gras, langoustines and artichoke|Lobster salad, tarragon and romesco|Sole fillets with mushrooms|Verbena soufflé, grapefruit sorbet|Petit Pasumot evening menu
price_range: Lunch 50-59 €; dinner menus 118 / 148 / 178 € (seen Oct 2026, Gault&Millau 2026 and Office de Tourisme); MICHELIN €€€€
reservation: Recommended (Office de Tourisme); book ahead for the auction weekend
notes: The three-course lunch menu (50 €), finishing on a soufflé
verdict: The MICHELIN page still shows one star after the 2026 selection, and Gault&Millau 2026 gives 13/20, calling the cooking bourgeois and regional, technically sure. Lunch at 50 € is the sensible way in; dinner climbs to 178 €. Diners' reviews note tables set close together and some noise, and one called the sole and the soufflé the high points of an otherwise uneven six courses.
caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday, no Tuesday lunch; book, the room is small and the tables close
hot_this_month: The three-course market lunch at 50 €, an autumn menu that changes with the market; lunch Wednesday to Saturday, dinner Tuesday to Saturday.

name: Clos du Cèdre
tier: THE SERIOUS DINNERS — TWO STARS INSIDE THE WALLS AND A CHARCOAL COUNTER
recognition: One MICHELIN star since the 2022 guide, still shown on its MICHELIN page after the France 2026 selection (16 March 2026)
what_to_order: Matured Charolais beef, bone marrow|Sole with shellfish and kasha risotto|Seasonal tasting menu|Burgundy from the hotel cellar
price_range: 95-190 € per person excluding drinks, about 150 € à la carte (Gault&Millau 2026, seen Oct 2026)
reservation: Book through the Hostellerie Cèdre & Spa (+33 3 80 24 01 01)
notes: Matured Charolais beef with bone marrow
verdict: The star dates from the 2022 guide (Yonder) and is still on the MICHELIN page after the 2026 selection. This is the more formal of Beaune's two starred rooms and the one that runs lunch at the weekend, which makes it the safer Sunday booking during the auction. Expect hotel-restaurant polish rather than surprise, and prices to match.
caveat: Dinner only Wed-Fri, lunch only at weekends; closed Mon-Tue (one gift listing); smart dress

name: Bissoh
tier: THE SERIOUS DINNERS — TWO STARS INSIDE THE WALLS AND A CHARCOAL COUNTER
recognition: Selected by Gault&Millau for 2026; MICHELIN inspectors have called the chef a 'master' (reported by Decanter)
what_to_order: Sumibi-yaki Limousin beef|Miyazaki wagyu|Eel grilled on binchotan|Grilled beef tongue|Sushi and tempura|Sake and lesser-known Burgundy
price_range: 45-63 € per person excluding drinks (Gault&Millau 2026, seen Oct 2026)
reservation: Book by phone; a counter of about ten seats
notes: Limousin beef aged 40 days, grilled over binchotan
verdict: Gault&Millau selected it for 2026 at 45 to 63 € a head before drinks, well under the starred tables, and the crowd of local winemakers says more than any guide. Reviews disagree on the food: some find the produce and tempura exact, others call portions thin. Go for the grill and the bottles, sit at the counter, and book: ten seats fill.
caveat: Dinner only, Wed-Sun; closed Mon-Tue; about ten seats, book

name: Ma Cuisine
tier: THE BOUCHONS — THE BURGUNDIAN CANON, COOKED STRAIGHT
recognition: Gault&Millau 2026: 12/20 in a sharing format; MICHELIN page: 'temporarily closed', undated
what_to_order: Galician beef|Pata negra|Prawns|Roast pigeon|Bottle from the regional cellar
reservation: Phone first to confirm it is open
notes: Whatever the cellar list suggests, with the Galician beef
verdict: Treat it as a call-first address this year. Gault&Millau's 2026 review (12/20) describes a working dinner room, but MICHELIN's page carries an undated 'temporarily closed' notice, and the February 2026 reopening in our old record was not found. If it is open, go for the cellar and a late booking; do not promise guests the old canon menu.
caveat: MICHELIN shows 'temporarily closed' (undated): phone before you plan on it; little wine by the glass

name: Le Bistrot Bourguignon
tier: THE BERTHS · THE BOUCHONS — THE BURGUNDIAN CANON, COOKED STRAIGHT
recognition: Selected by Gault&Millau for 2026, indicative 45 € per person
what_to_order: Oeufs en meurette|Bœuf bourguignon|Fish of the day|A bottle from the 600-reference list
price_range: About 45 € per person excluding drinks (Gault&Millau 2026, seen Oct 2026)
reservation: Recommended; reviewers say it fills quickly
notes: Oeufs en meurette, then the bœuf bourguignon
verdict: Gault&Millau keeps it in its 2026 selection at about 45 € a head before wine, which is honest money for the canon cooked properly. Reviewers say it fills fast and to come early if you have not booked. It is the straight answer to a guest who wants bourguignon in Beaune without the tourist-menu version.
caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday; small room that fills fast, book or come early
hot_this_month: Œufs en meurette, then the bœuf bourguignon, for the first cold nights; open Tuesday to Saturday, so not on Sunday 15 or Monday 16 November.

name: La Table du Square
tier: THE BOUCHONS — THE BURGUNDIAN CANON, COOKED STRAIGHT
recognition: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand shown on its MICHELIN page and in the Office de Tourisme's 2026 listing; Gault&Millau 12/20
what_to_order: Ferme de Clavisy lamb|Lamb confit|Fortnightly market menu|Desserts|Burgundy from an 800-reference cellar
price_range: 27-37 € per person excluding drinks (Gault&Millau, seen Oct 2026); 40 € menu reported by 2025 reviewers
reservation: Book ahead, especially Fri and weekends; reported 66 € charge for late cancellation
notes: The fortnightly market menu, with the Clavisy lamb if it is on
verdict: The best-value serious cooking on the boulevard, and the Bib on its MICHELIN page and in the 2026 tourist office listing backs that. Reviews also report a cool welcome and a strict booking policy, including a 66 € charge for cancelling inside twelve hours. Book ahead for Fridays and weekends, and confirm the penalty when you do.
caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday; cancellation inside 12 hours reported to cost 66 €

name: Le Comptoir des Tontons
tier: WINE ROOMS — THE BISTROTS WHERE THE BOTTLE COMES FIRST

what_to_order: Seasonal plate from organic-leaning produce|Pork from the kitchen|Natural wine to take away|Épicerie preserves from small producers
reservation: Call ahead; few seats and the table service is not confirmed for 2026
notes: Whatever the seasonal plate is, with a natural bottle chosen at the shelf
verdict: A Raisin visitor in mid-2026 praises the list and Pépita herself, so the house trades; whether the table service runs as it once did is less clear, since Raisin and Le Fooding now file it as a shop and TripAdvisor flags it closed. Treat it as a natural-wine cellar first, call to ask about a table, and expect conviction over polish: some reviewers find the service rough.
caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday per Pages Jaunes and Le Fooding; table service unconfirmed for 2026, call first

hot_this_month: Bao and small plates on its kitchen evenings, late in the week; listings disagree on which nights, so call before you plan the Friday of the auction weekend round it.

tier: LA RUE — THE SATURDAY MARKET, THE CHARCUTIER AND THE PÂTISSIER
recognition: Gault&Millau Pâtissier de l'année 2015 (then at the Park Hyatt Paris-Vendôme); listed in the Gault&Millau artisan guide at 18 rue Monge
notes: The cheesecake, the dish he brought from the Park Hyatt
verdict: Gault&Millau keeps him in its artisan listing and directory pages were updated in February 2026, but no review or post dated 2026 surfaced, so trading is likely rather than proven. The pastry is the reason to go; several reviewers find the service cool. The Sunday-morning opening makes it one of the few good stops on auction Sunday.
caveat: Closed Wednesday; Sunday mornings only; reviews mention cool, slow service
